rationaleAppend: Isaiah (isaiah-woh wave I-6, chapter 41 Editor; revised after review). The entry's Isaiah distribution paragraph names, among others, Isa 41:10, 41:13, 41:14, 43:1, 43:5, 44:2 and 54:4; the isaiah-woh lines render the opener 'Do not fear' at all seven (Isa 41 ASV 'Fear thou not' / 'Fear not', JPS 1917 and NJPS 'Fear not' / 'Have no fear'; Isa 54:4 ASV 'Fear not', NJPS 'Fear not'; checked 2026-11-27). The full formula with the presence clause, 'Do not fear, for I am with you', stands at 41:10 (ʾal-tîrāʾ kî ʿimmᵉḵā-ʾānî) and 43:5 (ʾal-tîrāʾ kî ʾittᵉḵā-ʾānî). At 41:13-14 ('Do not fear; I will help you'), 43:1 ('Do not fear, for I have redeemed you'), 44:2 ('Do not fear, O Jacob my servant') and 54:4 ('Do not fear, for you will not be ashamed') the opener carries another grounds clause or an address, and the line renders that clause as it stands, without supplying 'for I am with you'. Scope in Isaiah: absolute ʾal-tîrāʾ in a divine first-person oracle of assurance. Outside the entry: (i) the herald's plural exhortation at 35:4 (ʾal-tîrāʾû; chapter 35 Editor, signed off) and the herald's 'do not fear' at 40:9; (ii) the prohibitive with min + a named object of fear, which warns against a specific threat and is printed 'do not be afraid of …': the stable divine oracle 10:24 (ʾal-tîrāʾ ʿammî … mēʾaššûr, 'do not be afraid of Assyria') and, by the same rule, 37:6 (mippᵉnê haddᵉḇārîm, 'Do not be afraid of the words'; the chapter 37 Editor's site); (iii) other prohibitions of fear in the entry's list whose wording or setting differs (7:4; 8:12; 51:7; 54:14), left to their own chapters. 44:8 is not a site of this formula: its verbs are ʾal-tip̄ḥăḏû wᵉʾal-tirhû ('Do not dread, and do not be afraid'), not yrʾ; the entry's pairing of 44:8 with 'al-tira avdi Ya'aqov' belongs to 44:2. ISA-43:1, 43:5, 44:2 and 54:4 are stable lines whose English is unchanged.

Isaiah 41:14 (isaiah-woh wave I-6): wᵉgōʾălēḵ qᵉḏôš yiśrāʾēl 'and your Redeemer is the Holy One of Israel', the first occurrence of the divine title gōʾēl in the book; 'Redeemer' capitalised. ASV construes the clause as a predication (as the stable 54:5 does), and JPS 1917 and NJPS read apposition (checked 2026-11-27); the construal is recorded in the isaiah-woh overlay lexical-cruxes-isaiah-41.

Isaiah 41:18 (isaiah-woh wave I-6): territorial ʾereṣ ṣiyyāh 'the dry land' (ASV, JPS 1917; NJPS 'The arid land'; checked 2026-11-27), in parallel with midbār, keeps 'land' under the default. The universal idiom qᵉṣôṯ hāʾāreṣ 'the ends of the earth' at 41:5, 9 is governed by the isaiah-woh overlay eretz-cosmic-scope-isaiah-24.
